title: Undo on the canvas - paint first, masking too if it is not a refactor
description:
There is no undo anywhere on the canvas today - a grep for undo across js/ returns only comments. Every destructive stroke is permanent until Clear wipes the whole layer. That is survivable for a mask (a mask is a rough selection, and Detect/Points can regenerate it) and NOT survivable for paint, where one bad stroke over good work has no recovery short of starting again. MPI-375 is therefore the driver.

Proposed shape: a small command stack owned by MpiCanvas. One stroke (pointerdown to pointerup) = one command; Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z redo, bound through Hotkeys with ids in js/managers/hotkeyRegistry.js - never a raw keydown listener. Bounded depth.

MEMORY IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT, so decide it before coding: a full-layer RGBA snapshot at the 1536 max edge is roughly 9MB, so a 20-deep stack of snapshots is ~180MB per layer. Prefer dirty-rect patches (store only the bounding box a stroke touched, before and after) and fall back to whole-layer snapshots only for layer-wide operations like Clear.

MASKING IS CONDITIONAL, and the condition is explicit: extend it to masks ONLY if it is not a big refactor. MaskManager juggles four things (manualCanvas, subtractCanvas, autoPickMasks, selectedAutoPicks) plus the layer-ORDER rule fixed during MPI-371 (auto picks union LAST so a detection beats an older erase). If routing every mask mutation through commands means restructuring that, STOP and split the mask half onto its own card instead of growing this one.
acceptance: Undo and redo work for paint strokes in the paint tool, in stroke granularity
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z bound through Hotkeys with ids in hotkeyRegistry.js - no raw keydown listener
Stack depth is bounded and the memory cost per entry is measured and recorded, not guessed
The stack is cleared on entry switch and on tool teardown - no undo across two different images
Masking undo is either delivered in the same coherent pass or split onto its own card with the reason recorded - not half-wired
If masking is included: the MPI-371 layer-order rule (auto picks union LAST) still holds after an undo/redo sequence
